migrations: Heidi v2.1.7 adds database-backed MCP analytics, a hybrid coding benchmark, and compact terminal/LSP parity: migration 0018 persists restart-safe MCP-visible usage by unique event ID with current-week/current-month, rolling 7/30-day, and all-time aggregates; all 30 compact actions accept bounded self-reported client_model attribution without passing it to CPTR business handlers; cptr_benchmark runs owner-scoped standardized tasks with a server-owned randomized anti-tamper grader; cptr_terminal_control, cptr_lsp_read, and cptr_lsp_control expose the scoped interactive PTY/LSP backend without restoring legacy standalone production actions; observed real-work engineering metrics remain explicitly non-comparable; and the Workbench renders weekly/monthly estimated tokens, API-equivalent simulated cost, and benchmark evidence without storing prompts, source code, tool arguments, or tool results.

Heidi v2.1.6 hardens production execution prerequisites: Direct Coding reconstructs the active Heidi Python/Node runtime PATH even when service environment files are stale, production CPTR includes pytest/pytest-asyncio, host deployment provisions Managed Chrome with Ubuntu Snap support, and the default container image now includes Node/npm plus Chromium.

MCP v2.1.5 restores the bounded ChatGPT Apps Workbench on top of the unchanged 26-tool compact contract: production advertises exactly one MCP resource at ui://cptr/live-workbench.html, only cptr_open_live_workbench publishes ui.resourceUri, built UI assets ship in the signed release with hot reload disabled, and the widget refreshes a sanitized CPTR overview through a short-lived Workbench ticket instead of the CPTR service token.

CPTR v2.1.5 syncs audited heidi-dang/computer main commit a4a3a02251312e5f5c04b910d1e11857323b0ab5, including frontend polish, bulk model controls/search, and the extended API router surface while preserving Heidi-specific control-plane hardening.

MCP v2.1.4 made production release identity exact: the signed release manifest carries the source Git commit, production propagates and verifies that commit at runtime, the normal MCP build/HTTP surface was tool-only with the compatibility Workbench disabled, the legacy 69-action surface remained test-harness-only, and update metadata reported the deployed control profile.
MCP v2.1.3 makes cptr_open_live_workbench explicitly optional so normal ChatGPT Direct Coding starts with the task-relevant tool instead of a Workbench activation prerequisite.

MCP v2.1.2 splits mixed Workbench, SSH, managed Chrome, delegated task, and delegated monitor gateways into read and control surfaces so host safety annotations match capability while destructive/open-world controls remain conservative.
MCP v2.1.1 disables the MCP Apps UI entrypoint: no resources capability is advertised and no tool publishes ui.resourceUri metadata; Workbench session tools remain data-only.
MCP v2.1 adds cptr_workspace_lifecycle for zero-workspace create, clone, import, refresh, archive, and confirmed managed deletion.

The owner-full control profile is the deployment default for fresh installs and upgrades, adding command:external plus confirmed managed-workspace deletion; standard and developer remain explicit opt-down profiles, and legacy full remains an owner-full alias.
Git workspaces warm FDX automatically after provisioning; FDX failure remains a non-fatal fallback to normal CPTR Direct Coding.
Existing CPTR data under ~/.cptr is preserved; Heidi takes a pre-upgrade backup before activation.
FDX protocol 2 remains required for persistent structured resident reads.
